source.note: Scan without a text layer. National Senior Certificate paper (cover: NATIONAL SENIOR CERTIFICATE; running header: NSC). The PDF includes the cover (printed page 1), the instructions (page 2) and the information sheet (page 15); PDF page n = printed page n. The cover states that the question paper consists of 14 pages, 1 information sheet and a 25-page answer book. Duration 3 hours as printed on the cover. Source file and hash are recorded in sources/maths/manifest.json.

extraction.method: manual transcription from 170 dpi page renders, checked at 400 dpi where needed

questions.stem_md: The table below shows the total fat (in grams, rounded off to the nearest whole number) and energy (in kilojoules, rounded off to the nearest 100) of 10 items that are sold at a fast-food restaurant.

questions.text_md: Represent the information above in a scatter plot on the grid provided in the ANSWER BOOK.

questions.stem_md: The equation of the least squares regression line is  $\hat{y}=154{,}60+77{,}13x$.

questions.text_md: An item at the restaurant contains 18 grams of fat. Calculate the number of kilojoules of energy that this item will provide. Give your answer rounded off to the nearest 100 kJ.
Draw the least squares regression line on the scatter plot drawn for QUESTION 1.1.
questions.notes: Drawing the line needs two points calculated from the given equation.

questions.text_md: Identify an outlier in the data set.
Calculate the value of the correlation coefficient.
Comment on the strength of the relationship between the fat content and the number of kilojoules of energy.

questions.stem_md: A group of 30 learners each randomly rolled two dice once and the sum of the values on the uppermost faces of the dice was recorded. The data is shown in the frequency table below.

header: Sum of the values on uppermost faces

questions.text_md: Calculate the mean of the data.
Determine the median of the data.
questions.notes: Median of 30 values from a frequency table; no dedicated median skill, tagged with the five-number summary.

questions.text_md: Determine the standard deviation of the data.
Determine the number of times that the sum of the recorded values of the dice is within ONE standard deviation from the mean. Show your calculations.

questions.stem_md:
In the diagram below, the line joining  $\mathrm{Q}(-2\,;\,-3)$  and  $\mathrm{P}(a\,;\,b)$, $a$ and $b>0$, makes an angle of $45^{\circ}$ with the positive $x$-axis.  $\mathrm{QP}=7\sqrt{2}$ units.  $\mathrm{N}(7\,;\,1)$ is the midpoint of PR and M is the midpoint of QR.

Determine:

questions.text_md: The gradient of PQ
The equation of MN in the form  $y=mx+c$  and give reasons
The length of MN
The length of RS
questions.notes: RS = PQ as opposite sides of parallelogram PQRS (defined in 3.5). No dedicated parallelogram-properties skill.

questions.text_md: The coordinates of S such that PQRS, in this order, is a parallelogram
The coordinates of P

questions.stem_md: In the diagram below,  $\mathrm{Q}(5\,;\,2)$  is the centre of a circle that intersects the $y$-axis at  $\mathrm{P}(0\,;\,6)$  and S. The tangent APB at P intersects the $x$-axis at B and makes the angle $\alpha$ with the positive $x$-axis. R is a point on the circle and  $\mathrm{P}\hat{\mathrm{R}}\mathrm{S}=\theta$.

questions.text_md: Determine the equation of the circle in the form  $(x-a)^{2}+(y-b)^{2}=r^{2}$.
Calculate the coordinates of S.
Determine the equation of the tangent APB in the form  $y=mx+c$.
Calculate the size of $\alpha$.
Calculate, with reasons, the size of $\theta$.
questions.notes: Circle geometry (tan-chord or angle at centre) combined with the inclination found in 4.4.

questions.text_md: Calculate the area of $\triangle\mathrm{PQS}$.
questions.notes: Area from base PS on the $y$-axis and the perpendicular height from Q; no dedicated coordinate-area skill.

questions.stem_md: Given that  $\sin 23^{\circ}=\sqrt{k}$, determine, in its simplest form, the value of each of the following in terms of $k$, WITHOUT using a calculator:

questions.text_md: $\sin 203^{\circ}$
$\cos 23^{\circ}$

questions.stem_md: Simplify the following expression to a single trigonometric function:
questions.text_md: $\dfrac{4\cos(-x)\cdot\cos(90^{\circ}+x)}{\sin(30^{\circ}-x)\cdot\cos x+\cos(30^{\circ}-x)\cdot\sin x}$
Determine the general solution of  $\cos 2x-7\cos x-3=0$.
Given that  $\sin\theta=\dfrac{1}{3}$, calculate the numerical value of $\sin 3\theta$, WITHOUT using a calculator.

questions.stem_md: In the diagram below, the graphs of  $f(x)=\cos x+q$  and  $g(x)=\sin(x+p)$  are drawn on the same system of axes for  $-240^{\circ}\leq x\leq 240^{\circ}$. The graphs intersect at  $\left(0^{\circ}\,;\,\dfrac{1}{2}\right)$,  $(-120^{\circ}\,;\,-1)$  and  $(240^{\circ}\,;\,-1)$.

questions.text_md: Determine the values of $p$ and $q$.
Determine the values of $x$ in the interval  $-240^{\circ}\leq x\leq 240^{\circ}$  for which  $f(x)>g(x)$.
Describe a transformation that the graph of $g$ has to undergo to form the graph of $h$, where  $h(x)=-\cos x$.

questions.stem_md: A corner of a rectangular block of wood is cut off and shown in the diagram below. The inclined plane, that is, $\triangle\mathrm{ACD}$, is an isosceles triangle having  $\mathrm{A}\hat{\mathrm{D}}\mathrm{C}=\mathrm{A}\hat{\mathrm{C}}\mathrm{D}=\theta$. Also  $\mathrm{A}\hat{\mathrm{C}}\mathrm{B}=\dfrac{1}{2}\theta$,  $\mathrm{AC}=x+3$  and  $\mathrm{CD}=2x$.

questions.text_md: Determine an expression for  $\mathrm{C}\hat{\mathrm{A}}\mathrm{D}$  in terms of $\theta$.
questions.notes: Angle sum of the isosceles triangle ACD; no dedicated triangle-angle-sum skill.

questions.text_md: Prove that  $\cos\theta=\dfrac{x}{x+3}$.
questions.notes: Can also be done with the cosine rule in $\triangle\mathrm{ACD}$.

questions.text_md: If it is given that $x=2$, calculate AB, the height of the piece of wood.

questions.stem_md: Give reasons for ALL statements in QUESTIONS 8, 9, 10 and 11.
In the diagram below, cyclic quadrilateral ABCD is drawn in the circle with centre O.

questions.text_md: The angle subtended by a chord at the centre of a circle is … the angle subtended by the same chord at the circumference of the circle.
Use QUESTION 8.1.1 to prove that  $\hat{\mathrm{A}}+\hat{\mathrm{C}}=180^{\circ}$.

questions.stem_md: In the diagram below, CD is a common chord of the two circles. Straight lines ADE and BCF are drawn. Chords AB and EF are drawn.
questions.text_md: Prove that  $\mathrm{EF}\parallel\mathrm{AB}$.

questions.stem_md: In the diagram below, $\triangle\mathrm{ABC}$ is drawn in the circle. TA and TB are tangents to the circle. The straight line THK is parallel to AC with H on BA and K on BC. AK is drawn. Let  $\hat{\mathrm{A}}_{3}=x$.

questions.text_md: Prove that  $\hat{\mathrm{K}}_{3}=x$.
Prove that AKBT is a cyclic quadrilateral.
Prove that TK bisects  $\mathrm{A}\hat{\mathrm{K}}\mathrm{B}$.
Prove that TA is a tangent to the circle passing through the points A, K and H.
S is a point in the circle such that the points A, S, K and B are concyclic. Explain why A, S, B and T are also concyclic.

questions.stem_md: In the diagram below,  $\mathrm{BC}=17$  units, where BC is a diameter of the circle. The length of chord BD is $8$ units. The tangent at B meets CD produced at A.

questions.text_md: Calculate, with reasons, the length of DC.
questions.notes: Angle in a semicircle, then the theorem of Pythagoras.

questions.stem_md: E is a point on BC such that  $\mathrm{BE}:\mathrm{EC}=3:1$.  EF is parallel to BD with F on DC.

questions.text_md: Calculate, with reasons, the length of CF.
Prove that  $\triangle\mathrm{BAC}\;|||\;\triangle\mathrm{FEC}$.
Calculate the length of AC.
Write down, giving reasons, the radius of the circle passing through points A, B and C.
If the sides of two triangles are in the same proportion, then the triangles are …

questions.stem_md: In the diagram below, K, M and N respectively are points on sides PQ, PR and QR of $\triangle\mathrm{PQR}$.  $\mathrm{KP}=1{,}5$;  $\mathrm{PM}=2$;  $\mathrm{KM}=2{,}5$;  $\mathrm{MN}=1$;  $\mathrm{MR}=1{,}25$  and  $\mathrm{NR}=0{,}75$.

questions.text_md: Prove that  $\triangle\mathrm{KPM}\;|||\;\triangle\mathrm{RNM}$.
Determine the length of NQ.
